paper.core_task: Evaluating low-level visual perception, description, and quality assessment abilities of multimodal large language models

contributions.name: A benchmark for low-level perception with a new VQA dataset
contributions.author_claim_text: We build a benchmark for MLLMs on low-level perception ability. To achieve this, we construct a first-of-its-kind balanced and comprehensive LLVisionQA dataset with 2,990 images with one low-level-related question-answer pair for each image.
contributions.description: The authors construct the LLVisionQA dataset, a visual question answering benchmark specifically for low-level visual attributes, containing 2,990 images with questions covering multiple low-level concerns and question types.

contributions.name: A benchmark for low-level description with expert-labeled data and GPT
contributions.author_claim_text: We define a benchmark process to evaluate the low-level description ability of MLLMs, including an LLDescription dataset of 499 images with expert-labelled long golden quality descriptions, and a GPT-assisted evaluation to rate MLLM-descriptions in terms of completeness, preciseness, and relevance
contributions.description: The authors propose a benchmark process for evaluating low-level description ability, featuring an LLDescribe dataset with expert-written golden descriptions and a multi-dimensional GPT-assisted evaluation framework.

contributions.name: A softmax-based quality prediction strategy for MLLMs
contributions.author_claim_text: To evaluate precise quality assessment ability, we propose a unified softmax-based quality prediction strategy for all MLLMs based on their probability outputs.
contributions.description: The authors propose a softmax pooling strategy applied to the logits of 'good' and 'poor' tokens to extract quantifiable quality scores from MLLMs for image quality assessment.

novelty_claims.text: The paper lacks novelty as it primarily evaluates existing models without proposing new methods or techniques.
